title: Workflow concurrency block placement and the per-run placeholder opt-out
answers: where to put the concurrency block in a workflow
what concurrency placeholder to use when no grouping is needed
add concurrency to a workflow file
body:
Convention: the top-level `concurrency:` block sits after the `on:` trigger block and before `defaults:`, `env:` or `permissions:`. All 29 blocks added by this change follow that order.
Placeholder: when a workflow has no grouping decision yet, use `group: ${{ github.run_id }}` with `cancel-in-progress: false`. Each run gets its own group, so this stops concurrency-based cancellation and serialization between runs.
Constraints: this placeholder only satisfies the presence check in deny_workflow_without_concurrency. The PR states that meaningful grouping is a follow-up, so choosing a real group is a separate decision and should not be inferred from the placeholder.
applies: Adding or editing top-level workflow files in .github/workflows/*.yml; not composite action.yml files.
says: Workflow checks fail because a continuous integration file is missing the required concurrency setting
Where to place the concurrency configuration block in automated workflow files
Prevent concurrent workflow runs from canceling each other when grouping is not yet decided
Add a temporary concurrency placeholder to satisfy repository policy without delaying independent runs
New automated build pipelines require a concurrency definition to pass compliance checks
search: Top-level workflow files in `.github/workflows/*.yml` must place the `concurrency:` block after the `on:` trigger block and before `defaults:`, `env:`, or `permissions:`. When no grouping decision has been made, use placeholder `group: ${{ github.run_id }}` with `cancel-in-progress: false` to stop cancellation and serialization between runs. This placeholder only satisfies `deny_workflow_without_concurrency` in `.github/policy.rego`, applies strictly to top-level workflows rather than composite `action.yml` files, and does not define meaningful grouping.
